chunks: And from the evil of the sorceresses who blow incantations on knots
ai.seo_question: What does 'an-naffathat fi al-'uqad' mean in the Quran?
ai.summary: While the phrase 'min sharri annaffathati fi al-'uqad' is famously part of the morning and evening adhkars (supplications) derived from Surah Al-Falaq, its linguistic root connects to the narrative of Prophet Yaqub (AS) in Surah Yusuf (12:64) where he fears the evil of sorcerers. In Shia scholarly tradition, this phrase specifically denotes the practice of 'naffathat' (female sorceresses) who would blow incantations onto knotted cords to activate spells, symbolizing subtle, binding evils. It serves as a concise invocation for divine protection against both visible and hidden forces of magic that seek to entangle and harm the believer.
